description: Machine-readable feature state list. Single source of truth for scope. State transitions are gated by verification: a feature only becomes 'passing' when its verification command actually passes. See docs/FEATURES.md for rules.

features.behavior: CLI accepts `npx humb <database-url>`, auto-detects the database engine from the target (Postgres today), and starts the local server.
features.evidence: commit 9c37ec2 (PR #3): pnpm --filter humb test passes (7/7, packages/cli/src/index.test.ts) on 2026-07-01. Manually re-verified end to end against a real Postgres container: `HUMB_PORT=7799 humb <url>` listened on 7799 (env var previously silently ignored, now fixed via resolvePort), and `GET /` served the built apps/web UI (previously 404'd; fixed via static serving in packages/server) with `GET /api/health` reporting `connected`.

features.behavior: Launching Humb opens the browser UI which shows the database connection status.
features.evidence: commit ec9ebf2 (PR #6): pnpm test:e2e:full passes (1/1) on 2026-07-01 against a real Postgres container. Fixed a real infra gap along the way: Playwright's webServer only ran `vite preview` (no backend), so /api/health always failed - replaced with e2e/server.ts, which starts the real Humb server (API + built web app on one port, matching a real `npx humb <url>` launch) and connects to Postgres only when HUMB_TEST_DATABASE_URL is set.

features.behavior: Postgres adapter introspects schemas, tables, columns, indexes, and row counts.
features.evidence: commit 4ec7345 (PR #4): pnpm --filter @humb/db-postgres test passed (16/16) on 2026-07-01, including new integration tests (postgres-adapter.integration.test.ts) against a real Postgres container that previously did not exist for getOverview/getTable/getRows/runReadOnlyQuery. Auditing against the full spec found schemas/tables/columns were covered but indexes and row counts were entirely unimplemented (missing from @humb/core's TableMetadata contract and the adapter) - added IndexMetadata to @humb/core, index introspection via pg_index/pg_class/pg_attribute, and an approximate row count via pg_class.reltuples with a COUNT(*) fallback for never-analyzed tables (reltuples is -1 until ANALYZE runs). Manually re-verified end to end: GET /api/tables/public/humb_demo_users returned real indexes (with a genuine string[] columns array, not the raw Postgres array-literal string node-postgres returns for untyped array columns - caught and fixed via an explicit ::text cast) and rowCount 3. Package later renamed/moved packages/db-postgres -> packages/drivers/postgres (@humb/postgres) in commit cc3db12 (PR #5) as part of an architecture reorganization; re-verified the same 16/16 pass at the new location and updated this verification command accordingly.

features.behavior: UI shows a database navigation tree (schemas/tables) and table metadata.
features.evidence: commit ec9ebf2 (PR #6): pnpm test:e2e:full passes (1/1) on 2026-07-01: added SchemaTree/TableDetail components (@humb/ui), api/hooks (apps/web), wired into App.tsx. The connect-and-inspect journey now actually clicks the fixture table in the nav tree and asserts a column name is visible (previously only asserted the table name appeared as text, which would have passed without real interaction) - strengthened per the goal-driven-execution rule rather than leaving a superficial check.

features.behavior: UI displays a paginated page of rows for a selected table.
features.evidence: commit 1f779da: pnpm test:e2e:full passes (1/1) on 2026-07-01 against a real Postgres container: added RowsTable (@humb/ui), api/rows.ts + useRows hook (apps/web, using TanStack Query's keepPreviousData to avoid flicker between pages), wired into App.tsx below TableDetail with Previous/Next controls. "Can go next" uses a simple rows.length === pageSize heuristic (no exact total count from the backend) - manually verified the boundary is correct via curl with page=0/1 at pageSize=2 against the 3-row fixture. The connect-and-inspect journey now asserts real fixture row values (ada@example.com, grace@example.com) are visible, not just presence of a table.

features.behavior: Read-only SQL query runner executes SELECT-style statements and rejects mutations.
features.evidence: commit c049110: pnpm --filter @humb/postgres test (24/24) and pnpm --filter @humb/server test (8/8) pass on 2026-07-01. Auditing found a real, exploitable security bug: assertReadOnly only checked the leading keyword, so a writable CTE (`WITH deleted AS (DELETE FROM t RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM deleted`) starts with the allowed "with" keyword but actually deletes data - confirmed this executed a real DELETE through the adapter against a live table before fixing it. Fixed with two layers: assertReadOnly now scans the whole statement (literals/identifiers stripped first) for forbidden keywords anywhere, not just leading; and runReadOnlyQuery now runs inside a real Postgres READ ONLY transaction as the authoritative backstop - proved this independently with a test hiding a DELETE inside a plpgsql function call, which no string check could ever catch. Also fixed a rejected query returning HTTP 500 instead of 400 (moved ReadOnlyViolationError to @humb/driver-contract so packages/server can catch it without depending on a concrete engine). Built the missing UI (QueryRunner in @humb/ui, wired via apps/web) and manually verified success/rejection/writable-CTE cases through the real HTTP path against a live Postgres container.

features.behavior: Local server exposes health and runtime diagnostics endpoints for agent verification.
features.evidence: commit 5259102: pnpm --filter @humb/server test (8/8) and pnpm --filter @humb/postgres test (25/25) pass on 2026-07-01. Auditing /api/health (built in F001) against the full spec found a real bug, not just a coverage gap: node-postgres's Pool emits an unhandled "error" event when an idle client's connection is severed by the database (restart, network blip, admin kill) - confirmed live by starting the CLI against a real Postgres container, stopping the container mid-session, and watching the entire Node process crash instead of /api/health ever reporting "disconnected". Fixed by attaching pool.on("error", ...) in packages/drivers/postgres/src/index.ts's connect() to log instead of crash. Re-verified live: after the fix, killing the database leaves the server up and /api/health correctly returns database: "disconnected"; a subsequent SIGINT still shuts down cleanly. Added a regression test (postgres-adapter.integration.test.ts) that reproduces the exact failure via pg_terminate_backend on an idle pooled connection against a real database - confirmed it fails (uncaught exception) without the fix and passes with it.

features.behavior: CLI recognizes a SQLite file target (`npx humb ./app.db`) and the full connect-and-inspect journey (connection status, table list, columns, paginated rows, read-only query runner) works against it with zero credentials, per docs/product-specs/connect-and-inspect-sqlite.md. Also validates the driver-plugin architecture: a second engine is what actually proves packages/drivers/<engine> is reusable, not just designed to look reusable.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @humb/sqlite test && pnpm --filter humb test && pnpm test:e2e:full

features.behavior: README.md accurately reflects the current product (F001-F007 passing, not a skeleton), gives a working quick-start, and includes the marketing surface needed for GitHub/npm discovery: a demo GIF or asciicast, a "why not X" comparison section, badges (CI/npm/license), and the read-only-enforced-by-the-database security story from F006/F007.

`npm install -g humb` (or `npx humb@latest`) works standalone outside this monorepo: the published package serves the built apps/web UI (fixes the apps/web/dist monorepo-relative path tech debt tracked in docs/exec-plans/tech-debt-tracker.md), has npm-discoverability metadata (description, keywords, repository, homepage), and can be released via a repeatable script that bumps every publishable workspace package's version in lockstep and publishes them in dependency order.
